nodes.description: Immutable IERC20 liquidity asset escrowed by the FundingLocker.
Immutable address of the Loan that owns/controls this FundingLocker and is the only authorized caller.
Mapping owner[locker] => owner address, written with msg.sender in newLocker.
Mapping isLocker[locker] => bool flagging lockers created by this factory.
Constant factoryType = 2 identifying the FundingLocker factory.
Constructor storing the liquidity asset and loan addresses.
Loan-only function transferring liquidityAsset to an arbitrary destination via safeTransfer.
Loan-only function transferring the entire token balance to the loan via safeTransfer.
Modifier requiring msg.sender == loan, gating pull and drain.
Deploys a new FundingLocker owned by msg.sender and records it in owner/isLocker.
Attacker-controlled caller address used for authorization and ownership assignment.
External IERC20 token call in pull; token address is external and may execute arbitrary code before state is settled.
External IERC20 token call in drain; full-balance transfer to the loan address triggered by an external token contract.
Contract creation in newLocker using msg.sender as the loan parameter, making msg.sender the controller of the new locker.
Destination address parameter of pull, forwarded to safeTransfer.
Amount parameter of pull, forwarded to safeTransfer.
Local balance snapshot used as the transfer amount in drain.
Liquidity asset parameter used to construct the new FundingLocker.
Constructor parameter assigned to the immutable liquidityAsset state variable.
Constructor parameter assigned to the immutable loan state variable.

edges.reason: Modifier authorization depends on the attacker-controllable msg.sender being equal to the stored loan address.
The immutable loan address is the trusted comparison target inside the isLoan modifier.
isLoan gates entry into pull.
isLoan gates entry into drain.
pull executes an external token transfer before any accounting, enabling reentrant calls into pull.
The liquidityAsset token contract is the target of the external safeTransfer call.
Unvalidated dst parameter is passed directly as the transfer recipient.
Unvalidated amt parameter is passed directly as the transfer amount.
drain performs the full-balance external transfer, giving the token contract control flow.
liquidityAsset is both queried for balanceOf and used for the transfer in drain.
The loan address is used as the destination of the drained balance.
The local balance amount is used as the transfer value in drain.
A malicious liquidityAsset token can re-enter pull while the transfer is executing.
A malicious liquidityAsset token can re-enter drain during the balance transfer.
newLocker performs the FundingLocker contract creation.
msg.sender determines who becomes the owner of the newly created locker and is passed as the loan.
Caller-supplied liquidityAsset parameter flows into the FundingLocker constructor.
msg.sender is passed as the loan address, granting the caller full control over the new locker.
The new locker address is registered in the owner mapping with msg.sender as owner.
msg.sender value is written into the owner mapping.
The new locker address is flagged true in the isLocker mapping.
Constructor stores the liquidity asset into the immutable state variable.
Constructor stores the loan address into the immutable state variable.
Constructor parameter _liquidityAsset initializes the liquidityAsset state variable.
Constructor parameter _loan initializes the loan state variable.

normalization_plan.reason: The dst parameter is only used as the recipient argument of the external safeTransfer in pull.
The amt parameter is only used as the amount argument of the external safeTransfer in pull.
The local amt is just the balance snapshot feeding the external safeTransfer in drain.
The liquidityAsset parameter is only consumed by the FundingLocker contract creation.
The _liquidityAsset parameter is only used to initialize state inside the constructor.
The _loan parameter is only used to initialize state inside the constructor.
